answer: Because the onyx fee is applied at the lotus exit, the raven audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Withdrawing stake costs a 5% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 31 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
